en: Now, the Khilas; the first chapter.

Om, salutations to Viṣṇu. Now, regarding the purpose stated at the beginning of the Sūktas among the Khilas: [the description of] the presiding deities and the characteristics of the Śataghyā and others.
And there is an abundance of *chandas* (Vedic meters).

The *yajus* formulas consist of eighty syllables and so forth, increasing by four each time—namely, *kṛti*, *prakṛti*, *ākṛti*, *vikṛti*, *saṃkṛti*, *abhikṛti*, and *hrakṛti*. Regarding the number [of verses], in the case of sages who share the same name, the lineage (*gotra*) is not specified; as for the *khilas* (supplementary texts), the numbers and other details mentioned in the mantras themselves may apply.

1. → *Khila* 4.9. 2. There are four sacrificial formulas (*yajūṃṣi*): the *nivit*, the *purorucaḥ*, the *praiṣāḥ*, and the *kuntāpāḥ*. Then there is a triplet (*tṛca*) beginning with "śaśvat," followed by "pakvanā," "tākṣryaḥ," and "suparṇaḥ. That [section] belongs to the Aśvins. The seventh verse is addressed to Agni; the following one is addressed to Indra. The eleventh or the ninth has its deity indicated by the internal mark (*liṅgoktā*). From the eighth onwards are the *virāṭpāścastro* verses: the *jagatī*, the *urobṛhatī*, and the *pra sapta* verses. The *brāhmaṇa* sections include the *nipada* and *upanipada*; the second is a *jagatī*, and the sixth is in the *virāṭsthāna* meter. The *jyotirmatam* section consists of ten verses by Bhāradvāja Jyotiṣmat, five of which have deities indicated by their internal marks. The ninth and eleventh are in the *anuṣṭubh* meter. The *kṛśa* section (eleven verses) belongs to the Aśvins. The first six have deities indicated by their internal marks and are in the *anuṣṭubh* meter. These seven are the *apunardoṣa* verses. The next is addressed to Indra and Varuṇa, in the *jagatī* meter. This section of six verses is for the Renāgās. When it is a triplet, Yāmuni is the leader. The section of six verses beginning with "yam" is for Yajñatsoya. The group of four is by Gaurīviti. This section of eight verses concerns the two eyes and is addressed to the Aśvins. The final verse is a *jagatī*; those whose lineage (*gotra*) is not mentioned here belong to the Suparṇas.
1. "By the eighth [verse], the Virāj-foot consists of four [syllables]"—this is correct.
Having gazed upon the one of equal splendor, whose greatness is upward-turned and who is more powerful than the sun, I have taken unto myself the glory of the glorious ones and all forms.
Grant us a share of the Uryā river as a father divides his inheritance among his sons;
for you, O Sūrya, are the master of long life—bestow that upon us.
O you of infinite reach, great like Mitra, as you ascend, O far-seeing one—may we behold you for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns.
I have grasped that ram, invoked by many.
The *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.51.1 should be recited immediately after *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.50. [Variants]: *maiksamuller-āuṣa*; 1.

2. = *Taittirīya Āraṇyaka* 3.7.6.22; 22 = *Khila* 1.5.5; *dhehi-kā*; *dehi* in *Taittirīya*, *Maitrāyaṇī*, and *Āśvalāyana*. 31. = *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 1.50.11; *Taittirīya Āraṇyaka* 3.7.6.22. 32. = *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 7.66.16; *Atharvaveda* 19.67.1–2; *Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā* 4.9.20; *Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā* 36.24; *Taittirīya Āraṇyaka* 4.42.5; *Mānava Gṛhya Sūtra* 1.22.11; *Hiraṇyakeśi Gṛhya Sūtra* 1.7.10; *Pāraskara Gṛhya Sūtra* 1.11.9; *Mantrapāṭha* 2.5.13–14. 3. = *Khila* 1.5.6; → *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 10.37.7–8. 2.
O you who are invoked by many, the cows constantly sing of your true greatness, which is firmly established.
When you two, O Aśvins, brought Bhujyu to the setting [of the sun] in the supportless depth.
When you two, O Aśvins, brought the white horse to Abhitapas, and when you delivered Bhujyu with your favor like a boat;
that delight of yours, O Dastras, the inspired singers have proclaimed in the assemblies, seeking to reach it.
911 Supplements [Book 1, Supplement 2]: O you two praised by many, may you graciously accept our invitation; let your well-yoked swans carry you hither.
Like wives longing for their husbands, the hymns of praise attend you two, O youthful, bountiful, and powerful ones.
Come to us with your triple-seated chariot to the Soma-draught; pour forth the vessel for our exhilaration.
For you two the sacred grass is strewn and the sweet libations are prepared; the Hotṛ-priests, skillful-handed and masters of the chariot, are harnessed.
O Heaven and Earth, you two who provide clothing, who are variegated and the repositories of the world—O Rodasī, created by the Ordainer, hear my call!
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, with asses for steeds, come to my invocation together with Sūryā.
Let there be outpourings of honey and clarified butter; let them pour down the potent Soma with vigor.
In this way, may the youthful Aśvins milk forth strength for the arms with honey and clarified butter.
Let the ascetics praise at the beginning; let the hymns go forth toward that heavenly Gharma.
May the fourteenth, the triple-heavened youth, measure out vigor and wealth for those who are well-disposed.

I strike at Hari with compassion; O Purumīḷha, may I win the stalk, the bull, the bay-horsed one, the seven-horsed one, the one with three naves and well-fastened fellies—Varuṇa Pragātha for our well-being.
Soma, the greatness of Viṣṇu, and vital power—these the seers and the heroic men celebrate together.
The sons of Sudhanvan, skillful-handed, with their sacred labors [invoke] Tvaṣṭṛ, the Aṅgirasa, for our well-being.

Right here, O cloud-like one, I place for you that firm and intense Bṛhaspati within your heart. I bestow wealth upon you who possess the oblation; with sacred rites, they carry forth the one whose mind is focused.
The two eternal sons of Suparṇa, the all-pervading ones who guard the paths, the observers of men with threefold locks of hair and dark plumage—
this female crow, seeking protection, has awakened you as you were sleeping, for she was being tormented by a hawk.
I pierce with my shaft this wheel that has three naves, sixteen spokes, and a hundred felloes with twenty counter-spokes;
it has six sets of eight, is multiform, possesses a triple-pathed rim, and has delusion as its twofold cause.
He found the thirty-five-fold [soma] standing in a single enclosure, the ten-fold supreme;
he discovered the auspicious thirty-fold, the nine-cave [soma], and the sixty-eighth sacrifice.
The gods have established the bannered, virile, and heroic steed, the tawny one with beautiful hair, who bestows gifts.
May Indra, the sixteen-fold one, come and grant us protection; they call him the one who possesses sixfold armor, existing as a single unity.

These and eleven others are the *sauparṇa* hymns (*sūkta*). Likewise, here the deity is Brahmā (3.118–119): "For ever indeed yours... These ten are the *āśvina* hymns; they constitute a praise of Indra and Varuṇa.
"And whatever [goddesses] belonging to the lineage of Suparṇī are praised in the Nipāta hymns."
The *Ṛgvidhāna* (1.108) also states: "One desiring sons, cattle, wealth, heaven, and infinite life should practice the eleven purifying hymns dedicated to Suparṇa."

The sons of Manu, the active ones, have sped forth; the sons of Sudhanvan have attained immortality through their labors, their sacred rites, and their skillful deeds as doers of good. → *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* 7.15.12: May the *Ṛbhus*, the doers of good, the skillful-handed ones, be auspicious to us.

14. *dadhanvaṃ devāḥ* → *Ṛgveda-saṃhitā* 8.19.1. 14. → *Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā* 26.10; *Taittirīya-saṃhitā* 1.4.41: "May the great Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, the sixteenfold one, grant us protection.
Let the streams of honey and clarified butter flow forth, which the two wise ones found for the sake of growth."

Mitra and Varuṇa, the makers of the world; may those Aśvins enjoy my libation. (1) [The chariot] easy to mount, swift-moving, reaching a hundred goals, rapid, auspicious, and golden, which comes on the morning journey.
Mount [your chariot], O daughter of Virūpa; we make you our helper.
Those two who are the axle-protectors of the chariot, the wise ones, swift as the wind, well-yoked, and dripping with clarity—[mount them].

With those [powers] wherewith you come to the bridegroom’s choice, O Sūryā, with those, O Dastrās, strengthen us in battles. Whatever seed of yours, O Aśvins, is nourishing, or whatever the bull [bestowed] upon Vadhrimatī, O bounteous givers.
Since the wise one, desiring the gods and highly skillful, offered this to her, the two physicians have joined it with care.
O Nāsatyas of wondrous luster, that medicine by which you protected Ghoṣā when she longed for offspring— [grant that to us].
May that gift given to her by three husbands, through which she obtained this skillful handiwork, be hers.
O Dastras, O Nāsatyas, let the wise Hotṛ priest offer the *vaṣaṭ* call to you both at this pressed juice.
May she who has given birth without pain praise you; may she who has given birth at the joint [of the body] deliver her offspring.
Thus, O wise ones, this secret doctrine (upaniṣad) is for you two, the well-yoked, fair-winged daughters of Rebha.
"O Śakra and Agni, bestow upon those who know the sacrifice the rams and their offspring, even the tortoise. (RV 10.92.14).

This hymn is indicated in the middle of Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.12.14; Aitareya Āraṇyaka 6.25.7; and 8.10.4. In Sāyaṇa’s commentary: "The 'Sauparṇa-hymn' begins with the verse, 'May the wise ones come forth with honey... (RV 10.92.14).

O Kuśa, Lord of the World, you are the wondrous master of the gods. O Aśvins, Nāsatyas, protect us; let your sacrifice pass beyond our enemies. (1) You, the fair-winged one, brought him from heaven; the sons of the gods have settled here. Agni Jātavedas has become the lord of creatures, O far-seeing one. (2) Agni is the Hotṛ, the pervasive Vasu, the highest glory of the gods. Again, Agni is Prajāpati, Vaiśvānara, the golden one. (3) May Agni be our protector, auspicious, beautiful, and for all [beings]. Protect us from every side with double wealth—O Soma-drinker, the bringer of fearlessness! (4) O Agni, drive away the afflictions of our vital organs and the secret wounds of our enemies. You are the master of long life; bestow that upon us, O Sūrya! (5) O Mitra-like one of great luster, rising up, O far-seeing one, may we behold you for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns. (6) You two, O Aśvins, have made the sage Kuśa, who was worn out and aged, young again through your deeds—him who was unyielding, withered like a small flower, fierce, yet now youthful again, the husband of maidens. (7) O powerful ones, he who honors you with Soma, with the threefold hymn, with clarified butter, with sacred knowledge, or with his mind—he gains radiant treasure, accompanied by Indra, much-desired, victorious in battle, and possessed of brave sons. (8) O heroes, the one who holds all wealth, inspired by thought, sends forth the mountain for you two now. He sends the trees, the ocean, and the youthful one; then make him full of abundance. (9) The one who holds all wealth, the skillful-handed, the swift, the noble, the peerless, the towering one, has called out. Like the wielder of the thunderbolt seeking the light of heaven, he has shattered the tree of this one. (10) Thus, O Kuśa, the prayer is being recited; may the gift be easy to invoke. For the sake of increasing your strength, I have fashioned these prayers; grant us, O giver of gifts, the fulfillment of our desire. (11)

920. Supplements [Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1.6]: These portions of yours flow forth, O Indra and Varuṇa; for you two are great at the pressed juices.
At every sacrifice, you who delight in the alliance, you take pleasure when you bestow your favor upon the sacrificer who presses the soma.
1 | O Indra and Varuṇa, the waters, which ward off hostility and bestow prosperity, have attained your greatness—
those two who cross over the path at the far limit of the mid-region, and before whom no enemy can stand as long as they are awake.

2 | O Indra and Varuṇa, it is true that the cloud, dripping with clarity, milks forth the seven voices as its wave. With these, O Lords of Splendor, protect the one who bestows nourishment— he who watches over you both with his thoughts.
3 | The seven sisters, the sweet ones who drink ghee and give quickly, dwell in the seat of Cosmic Order (ṛta).
O Indra and Varuṇa, with those [streams] of yours that drip with ghee, bestow skill upon the sacrificer.
4 | We have proclaimed the true majesty and Indra-like power of those two for great good fortune.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you who hear the clarified butter, protect us with three hundred [aidings], O lords of splendor!
5 | O Indra and Varuṇa, when from the inspired thoughts of the sages you first established the understanding of speech and the sacred hearing,
the wise ones released those meters while performing the sacrifice; through austerity, they beheld them.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon the sacrificers a mind of goodwill and the increase of wealth;
grant us progeny, nourishment, and riches, and extend our lifespan for the sake of long life.

The elision of the penultimate vowel is a Vedic license (*chāndasa*).

[She is] "Hiraṇyaprākārā," meaning she whose enclosure or covering (*prākāra*) is gold (*hiraṇya*), that is, gold or refined metal; or alternatively, she whose form or appearance (*prakṛṣṭa ākāraḥ ākṛtiḥ*) is golden.
She is *ārdrā*, meaning moist, because she was born from the Ocean of Milk;

In this context, the word "Rudra" begins with a nasalized vowel (*mūrdhanya*).
Because it is seen thus in cases such as *ārdrā* and *hadra*; otherwise, it is due to the rule of diversity (*bāhulaka*).
[She is] blazing, that is, shining.
Satisfied and joyful, yet satisfying the desires of her devotees—this is the implied sense. Seated upon a lotus, meaning resting or sitting on a lotus.
Lotus-colored, meaning having the hue of a lotus.
I call hither—that is, I summon near—her who is well-known as Śrī.

In this context, the insertion of the word *arhat* immediately after *pra padye* is a scribal error. *Candrām*: shining like the moon; *prabhāsām*: she whose radiance (*bhāḥ*) or beauty is preeminent. *Āpa ca eva*: [the syllable] *āp*. *Yaśasā jvalantīm*: blazing or shining with fame and renown. *Loke khaloke devajuṣṭām*: in this world and in the other world, she who is cherished or served by the gods and others, or she who is pleased. *Udārām*: generous, munificent, or eloquent. *Padminīm*: having the form of a lotus-creeper, or shaped like a lotus. *Īm*: this particle is meaningless, according to Yāska’s statement: "In short compositions, *kam*, *īm*, and *idu* are meaningless" (Nirukta 1.9). Alternatively, it may signify that which is expressed by the vowel *ī*. *Tām śriyam*: that Śrī. *Loka iha loke śaraṇam*: as a refuge or protector in this world. *Pra padye*: I take refuge in; the word *aham* (I) is to be supplied. That cruel magic spell (*kṛtyā*) which our enemies fashion like a bride, that we drive away with sacred prayer (*brahman*); let it go to destruction. 1. The head-turning, ear-piercing, multiform, terrifying one—whom I have sent forth, O Heart, you who possess the three principles, join her with misfortunes. 2. With whatever thought you perceive the malevolent deeds of the wicked, turn that very thing back upon them; do not harm us, who are sinless. 3. O Fire, turn back the maker; he has been cast out by our power. Turn back his life, O Consumer of Men, and his progeny. 4. To him who fashioned you here as a spell, go back to him, O New One! Destroy the enemies, the spell, and all sorceresses (*yātudhānī*). 5. Quickly, O Spell, return to the house of the maker himself! Destroy his cattle and his dwelling, and strike down his heroic sons. 6. Whosoever, knowing or unknowing, sends you toward our homes, from him you shall depart swiftly; make his body full of sores. 7. May the radiant Vedic prayer (*brahman*) drive you back, the slayer of enemies; and may Agni, the slayer of demons, the slayer of foes, and the one-footed Ekapāt, drive you away. 8. Just as the ancient Aṅgirases, the Bhṛgus, the Atris, and the Vasiṣṭhas drove you back, even so do we drive you back. 9. He who joined your limbs together with wisdom, as if the joints of a chariot—go to him, there is your people; this person here is unknown to you. 10. Whoever, whether standing in battle or elsewhere, seeks to harm us—you, O Arrow, know him; pierce his body as he is provoked. 11. O God, be swift against the hater of the gods; O Spell, consume the evil-doer; let nothing of him remain. 12. By those paths of ours which lead to distant lands, send our enemies and the spell far away; turn them back. 13. Whoever, an enemy or a foe, seeks to injure us even in thought—whether he be far off or near at hand, drink the heart’s blood of that one. 14. With whatever heart you were sent as a spell with the intent to kill us, let the autumnal thunderbolt, both piercing and non-piercing, destroy that heart. 15. Whether you approach us as a two-footed woman or as a four-footed beast, driven away and stripped of vows by us, go to the eight-footed house of the maker. 16. Whoever curses us, or whoever curses one who curses us—he, like a tree struck by lightning, shall wither away root and branch. 17. Him whom we hate, and he who hates us, the sinful one who seeks to curse us—I hurl him, like a die in the gambling hall, to Death. 18. Whatever curse comes from a rival wife, whatever curse from a sister-in-law, and whatever a Brahmin curses in anger—all that is the weapon of the spell. 19. Whether he be a kinsman or a stranger who seeks to injure us—you, having stepped upon him, shatter his head as Vishnu does. 20. O Thousand-eyed Fire, go forward; yoke the swift chariot of the curse. Seek out the enemies, O Spell; having seized them, bring them to their unbarred homes. 21. Enclose us from the curse as a cowherd encloses his herd; strike down the enemies as the celestial thunderbolt strikes the trees. 22. Drive my enemies away from the curse, and likewise the spells and the malicious friends. May the tongues of the wicked be smooth, yet let them be consumed by the kindled Jātavedas. 23. Make me free from rivals in the east, auspicious in the south; grant me constant fearlessness in the west and in the northern home. 24. Go away, O Spell; do not stay. Lead him to his own place; for you are the hunter of the deer, and you ought to destroy him. 25.

(2) Whether it was done with a staff, or with an arrow, or with wood, or by a weapon—of that you are the remedy. Having provided the remedy on your summit, O herb! (3) You fly from tree to tree like a maiden acting like a bull. Conquering and standing firm, you are indeed named Saṃjeyā. (3) May that which was improperly spoken by me find rest; may I be able to recite what I have studied. May I comprehend what has been comprehended; may what I have heard remain within me. Agni is the god who bestows wealth; Agni is the one who knows all things; Agni is the excellent preparer of the sacrifice. He is the invoker chosen by the gods; he is the invoker chosen by Manu. He is the leader of wisdom, the charioteer of the sacrifices. He is the swift invoker, for he is rapid in his course. May the god bring the gods hither—Agni, the god who knows the gods. May he, the knower of all beings, perform the sacrifices. May Indra, the great one, drink of the Soma; he whose praise is the Maruts, whose host is the Maruts, whose friends are the Maruts, and whose strength is the Maruts. May he, together with the power of the Maruts, drive away the Vṛtras and release the waters. The gods rejoiced in him when, in the battle against Vṛtra where the sun was hidden, he slew Śambara.

980. [Khila 9, Anuvāka 5] In the *hatya* and *gaviṣṭha* hymns, they sing praises with secret words in the furthest distance. Increasing his sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*), making them unassailable by his might, and performing service for the gods, Indra, accompanied by the Maruts as his friends—may he hear us here; may he drink of the Soma here. May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom. May he favor this priestly power (*brahma*), may he favor this noble power (*kṣatra*). May he favor this sacrificer who presses the juice. With his wondrous aids, may the Wondrous One hear us; through his protection, may he come to our prayers. 2.

May the god Indra drink the Soma; he who is the most heroic among those born once, the strongest among those born many times; the rider of the two bay steeds, the offspring of Pṛśni; the wielder of the thunderbolt, the destroyer of forts, the shatterer of forts; the creator of the waters, the leader of the waters, the leader of living beings; the slayer of the lords of the distant regions, the provider of nourishment, the possessor of wealth; the god who has come here seeking this [sacrifice]. May the god Indra hear us here; may he drink the Soma here. May the god protect this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom. May he protect this sacred prayer (*brahman*), may he protect this sovereign power (*kṣatra*). May he protect this sacrificer who presses the juice. With his wondrous aids, may the Wondrous One hear us; through his protection, may he come to our prayer. 3.

May the divine Savitṛ, the golden-handed, fair-tongued, strong-armed, and well-fingered, drink of the Soma. May he, whose pressings are true, come thrice today. Wherein both the bestowers of life and the providers of sustenance, the two who delight in the impulse, have impelled the most excellent gift of Savitṛ: a milch-cow that yields milk, a draft-ox that draws the load, a swift steed, a victorious chariot-warrior, a bountiful mate for union, a youth fit for the assembly, one who drives away disease and one who drives away the reviler. May the divine Savitṛ hear us here; may he be exhilarated here by the Soma. May the god protect this invocation of the gods with his divine wisdom. May he protect this enclosure, may he protect this dominion, and may he protect this sacrificer who presses the Soma. May the Wondrous One, with his wondrous aids, hear us; may he come with his protective favor toward our prayer. 4.

May Heaven and Earth rejoice in the Soma; the Father and the Mother, the Son and the Procreative Power, the Cow and the Bull, the Dhanyā and the Dhiṣaṇā, the one rich in seed and the one easy to milk, the source of bliss and the source of delight, the full of vigor and the full of milk, the bestower of seed and the one who contains the seed—O Heaven and Earth, hear this here, rejoice in the Soma here! Protect this divine invocation to the gods with divine wisdom! Protect this sacred prayer (brahman), protect this sovereign power (kṣatra)! Protect this sacrificer who presses the Soma, O you two of wondrous aids, with your wondrous protections! Come to us with your favor, you who are renowned for your devotion to the sacred word. 5.

The Ṛbhus, the gods, have exhilarated themselves with Soma; having performed their work with skillful hands, they are deft in action. They are most blessed, most wealthy, most diligent in labor, and most powerful through their might. They who protected the cow Viśvabhū, the omniform—she became the omniform cow. O you whose vow is not for youth, [protect] the two bay steeds; come, O gods, to the sacrifice. Having awakened, they sang together; in a year’s time, the skillful ones attained their share of the sacrifice. The Ṛbhus, the gods, have heard us here; here let them exhilarate themselves with Soma. May these gods favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought. May they favor this spiritual power (*brahman*), may they favor this sovereign power (*kṣatra*), and may they favor this sacrificer who presses the Soma. Wondrous ones, with wondrous aids, may they hear us and come with protection through our prayer.

May all the gods rejoice in the Soma; all those belonging to Vaiśvānara; all those of universal splendor; great ones, mighty; they who are like the *takman* disease in the *nemadhitī* sacrifice; the swift ones, the carriers of the cooked offerings; those whose breath is the wind, impelled by fire; who have pervaded both heaven and earth; the waters and the sky; the *brahman* and the *kṣatra*; the sacrificial grass and the altar; the sacrifice and the atmosphere; you who are the three times eleven, the thirty-three, the three hundred and three. Fifth Chapter, Section 9, Verse 81.

A thousand [are you]; so many are your approaches, so many your arrivals at the gift-offering, so many your wives, so many your mothers, so many in your departure, so many in your settling. Therefore, O gods, you are more numerous than this. Let me not, O gods, be excluded from your praise, nor from your supreme praise. May all the gods hear us here; may they rejoice here in the Soma. May the gods favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought. May they favor this spiritual power (*brahman*), may they favor this sovereign power (*kṣatra*). May they favor this sacrificer who presses the Soma—wondrous ones with wondrous aids. Hearing us, may they come with their protection through devotion to the *brahman*. 7.

Agni Vaiśvānara, may he exhilarate himself with Soma; he is the kindler of the All-Gods, the eternal divine light that has shone for human generations. Flashing forth among those ancient ones, undecaying in the presence of the dawns, he who illumines the sky and the earth, the wide mid-air—may that light grant protection for the sacrifice. May Agni Vaiśvānara hear us here; may he exhilarate himself with Soma here. May this god favor this invocation of the gods with his divine wisdom. May he favor this spiritual power (*brahman*), may he favor this sovereign power (*kṣatra*), and may he favor this pressing sacrificer. With his wondrous aids, may he hear us and come to us with his protecting favor.

The Maruts, the gods, have exhilarated themselves with Soma—well-praising, well-singing, hymning with chants, possessing great vital strength, heroes, invincible, brilliant, sons of Pṛśni, splendid, wearing golden rings, powerful, seeking what is praiseworthy, dwelling in the clouds, and clothed in rain. May the Maruts, the gods, hear us here; may they exhilarate themselves here with Soma. May these gods favor this invocation of the gods with divine thought. May they favor this spiritual power (*brahman*), may they favor this sovereign power (*kṣatra*). May they favor this pressing sacrificer. Wondrous ones, with wondrous aids, may they come to hear us with their protection for our prayer. 9.

May Agni Jātavedas be exhilarated by Soma—Agni who is self-luminous, of wondrous radiance, the never-absent lord of the household, visible even through the darkness, worthy of praise, to whom the oblation of clarified butter is offered, whose paths are many, the performer of sacrifice, the invincible conqueror of enemies through his own power. O Agni Jātavedas, bestow upon us splendor and strength; protect the one who kindles you and the praiser from distress. May Agni Jātavedas hear us here; may he be exhilarated by Soma here. May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom. May he favor this spiritual power (*brahman*), may he favor this sovereign power (*kṣatra*), and may he favor this sacrificer who presses the juice. With your manifold aids, O wondrous one, may he hear our prayer and come to us with protection. 10.
In the exhilaration of this Soma, O singer, Indra shall rejoice; in the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra slew the dragon;
in the exhilaration of this, O singer, Indra slew Vṛtra.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra set in motion the rush of the waters.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra gave life to the sluggish, he helped the slow, and he strengthened the unconquered.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra caused the sun to rise; he subdued the Dāsa tribes and established them.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra held up the unbridled [mountain] and spread out the earth.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra set the sun in heaven and extended the mid-air. In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra brought the agitated oceans to rest.
In his exhilaration, O singer, Indra leaped like a wild bull; in his exhilaration, he brought to rest the agitated mountains.
In his exhilaration, O singer, may Indra here find glory; here let him be intoxicated by the soma. May the god favor this invocation of the gods with divine wisdom.
May Brahman protect this; may Kṣatra protect this;
may it protect the one who presses the soma and the sacrificer, with its various aids.
May he go to the dwelling of the one who hears the sacred word.

(3) O divine Adhvaryus, come on your chariot bright as the sun; anoint the sacrifice with honeyed mead. I have uttered speech that is pleasing and honeyed, in the invocations of the gods. Through speech I have attained greatness; through speech I have attained peace; through speech I have attained immortality. Through speech I have attained this; through speech he has attained this. Well-adorned; well-adorned—thus in the manuscript (mu).
In the *su*-manuscript, the sixth mantra is read as the sixth and seventh, and the seventh is read as the eighth.
7 [1] The Chapter on Directions (*praipādhyāya*).

(a) Let the Hotṛ worship Agni, who has been well-kindled with excellent fuel at the navel of the earth, in the gathering place of the waters, at the height of heaven—the one praised by all. O Hotṛ, sacrifice the clarified butter!
(Ā) Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Tanūnapāt, the offspring of Aditi, the guardian of the world;
let the god, for the sake of the sacrificial offering, anoint the divine ones on the path of the gods—O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter of all! Vaishvājyasya hotaryaja!

(i) Let the Hotṛ worship Narāśaṃsa, the one praised by men, the leader of men. May he be rich in cattle, powerful with wealth, preeminent with chariots, radiant with gold—O Hotṛ, sacrifice for the sake of the Vaiśvājya butter!
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni. Being praised, may the god, being implored, bring hither the gods as his messengers, he who is the bearer of oblations and free from delusion.
May he come to this sacrifice; may the god protect this invocation of the gods. O Hotṛ, perform the offering of the Vaiśvājya butter.
(e) Let the Hotṛ worship the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), well-spread and providing a covering, at this sacrifice; let it extend threefold and wide for the welfare of the gods.
O Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, sit upon this dear seat of Indra. O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter belonging to all.
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice. Let the lofty ones, the two Kaṣā, the daughters of Kūpadhāvan, rise up with their uplifted [limbs]. Let them rest upon the three sides;
let them, easy of access, rest upon the three at this sacrifice. Let those who increase Truth partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
(o) Let the Hotṛ worship Dawn and Night, the lofty, well-adorned ones, who prepare a womb for the *pañkti* verses.
As they sit together with Indra and the gods, let them sit upon this sacrificial grass (*barhis*) and enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
The supplements (khilāni): May the Hotṛ worship the divine Hotṛs, the two delightful ones, the Potṛs, the two sages who are wise.

May the two goddesses, Strīṇā and Madyā, with their own impulsion and by their own power, place this sacrifice in heaven among the gods, approved by themselves; let them partake of the sovereignty; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! The Hotṛ shall sacrifice: may the two goddesses, most excellent in their work, stand here; may they extend this sacrifice;
may the goddesses partake of the divine waters and of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
(a: Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ—the most brilliant, the one who is not unwise, the bestower of seed, the one who extends to all, the bestower of glory;
the one of many forms, visible at will. May he be well-nourished with nourishments and possessed of good heroes through his heroes. O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter!
(ka) Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, the one who dwells near, the one who destroys enemies, the lover of the sacrifice, whom men have served.
May the axe cut [the wood] for itself; may the season, the god who carries the oblation to the gods, partake of the clarified butter.

O Hotṛ, sacrifice! (kha) Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni with *svāhā* for the clarified butter, *svāhā* for the marrow, *svāhā* for the drops, *svāhā* for the *svāhā*-utterances, and *svāhā* for the hymns of the oblation.
*Svāhā*! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, come to the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
7 [2] (a) Agni has won the prize; the god, the bearer of oblations to the gods, has prevailed.
Being praised by the wise with their songs, he prepares the life-span of the sacrifice.
O Hotṛ, proceed further and further, bringing the oblations to the gods.
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; may he enjoy the clarified butter, O Hotṛ, at this sacrifice.
Let the Hotṛ worship Soma; may he enjoy the oblation, O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice.
(u) Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni and Soma; may they enjoy the omentum and the fat of the goat; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the oblation!
(e) Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni and Soma; may they enjoy the sacrificial cake; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the oblation!

(ai) Let the Hotṛ worship Agni and Soma; let them both partake today of the goat-offering. Let them consume the fat extracted from the middle, before the onset of hatred, before the human seizure. Now, let them eat of those [goats] that have fed on fodder, that have grazed first upon the pasture, that flow with excellent milk, belonging to the hundred Rudras, whose meat is not mixed, who are clothed in fatness—from the flanks, from the blood, from the marrow, from every limb, let them take the portions offered. May Agni and Soma indeed act thus; may they enjoy the oblation. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! (o) O Vanaspati, you whose leaves are golden, bring the oblations to the gods; from of old, your purpose is for this end.
Having bound him with a girdle turned to the right, lead him along the straightest paths of Cosmic Order.
Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, for he has been fastened with a girth that reaches to his shoulder.

Where the dear abodes of Agni’s oblation of clarified butter are, where the dear abodes of Soma’s oblation of clarified butter are, where the dear abodes of the goat-oblation for Agni-Soma are, where the dear paths of Vanaspati are, where the dear abodes of the gods who drink clarified butter are, where the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ are—there he has placed this [oblation], as if having leveled it and smoothed it out; having made it as if easy to approach, let the divine Vanaspati offer the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! [Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 5.7]. Fifth Adhyāya. 989.
O Lord of the Forest, having bound [the victim] with a cord, you who know the ritual procedures made of flour, carry the oblations to the gods; and do you proclaim the giver among the immortals.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. Let him worship the dear abodes of Agni, the oblation of clarified butter; let him worship the dear abodes of Soma, the oblation of clarified butter; let him worship the dear abodes of Agni and Soma, the oblation of the goat; let him worship the dear paths of Vanaspati; let him worship the dear abodes of the gods who drink clarified butter; let him worship the dear abodes of Agni, the Hotṛ. Let him worship your greatness. May he sacrifice these offerings; may Jātavedas prepare the nourishments for the sacrifice and accept the oblation. O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!

This sacrificer has chosen you, Agni, as the Hotṛ priest—preparing the cooked offerings, preparing the *puroḍāśa*, taking the portions for the clarified butter, and bringing the clarified butter for Soma, and the goat for Agni and Soma. The divine Vanaspati has become well-disposed; with the clarified butter he has bestowed [the offering] upon Soma, and with the goat he has bestowed it upon Agni and Soma. They have accepted him through the fat; they have both increased him with the *puroḍāśa*. And you, O seer, descendant of seers, grandson of seers, this sacrificer has chosen you from among many who have gathered together.

"May this wealth, the best of things, be unimpaired among the gods. Recite those divine gifts which the gods have bestowed; announce them to him and proclaim them, O Hotṛ, for the one who desires blessings and speaks auspicious words. Sent forth by man, speak the hymns for the Sūktavāka.

7 [3] (a) May the divine *barhis* be well-disposed toward the gods, rich in heroes through the heroes. May it be spread at dawn and held firm at evening. May we, possessing the *barhis*, rejoice in wealth. For the winning of wealth, may he partake of the gift of treasure. Sacrifice!

(ā) O divine Doors! Open wide at this gathering; here is Agni, firm and steadfast at the invocation of the gods. May the young calf, or a newborn boy, measure out these [doors]. Let not the dust-stirring horse pass them by. Let them enjoy the gift of wealth in the world of the living; sacrifice! (i) O divine Dawn and Night! May you both attend this sacrifice. Truly, the divine hosts have arrived. Well-pleased and well-disposed, let them partake of the gift of wealth in the world of the living; sacrifice!

(u) The two divine consorts, the bestowers of wealth, of whom one drives away hostilities and the other brings desirable things to the sacrificer—may they both partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the distribution of riches; sacrifice to them. (e) The two divine offerings of strength (*ūrjāhutī*): may one bring nourishment and strength, and the other the union and the shared draught; may we be favored by the new through the old, and by the old through the new. May those two offerings of strength, being strengthened, bestow that strength upon us; may they both partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the distribution of riches; sacrifice to them.

(ai) The divine gods, the two divine Hotṛs, Potṛs, Neṣṭṛs, and the two who destroy the evil speaker—may they both partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the distribution of riches; sacrifice to them.

(o) Three goddesses, three goddesses: Ilā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī. Whomsoever Bhāratī has touched along with the Ādityas, Sarasvatī with the Rudras, and Ilā with the Vasus at the sacrifice—may we rejoice in their company. May they partake of the offering for the gain of wealth and the bestowal of riches; sacrifice! (au) The god Narāśaṃsa, three-headed and six-eyed, holds these hundred white-footed ones; they carry him forth by the thousand. Bṛhaspati is worthy of the office of Hotṛ for Mitra and Varuṇa, Aśvin the office of Stotr, and Aśvin the office of Adhvaryu. May he accept the offering for the gain of wealth and the bestowal of riches; sacrifice!

The divine tree, the rain-shelter, dripping with clarity, has reached the firmament; it has protected the two worlds from within and has firmly established the earth with its foundation. May it partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining riches; sacrifice!

The divine *barhis* of the water-plants, the most excellent among those that spread out, the bestower of all desires, the protector of many, the glorious one—through this sacred grass, may we overcome our enemies. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let it partake; sacrifice!

(Agni) Sviṣṭakṛt, the divine, the joyous, the wise seer, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing priest—O Agni, Hotṛ, more worthy of sacrifice than the Hotṛ-priest himself, those gods whom you have sacrificed to and whom you have gratified, they have rejoiced in your office as Hotṛ.

May we, together with them, offer this sacrifice to the gods in heaven through this Hotṛ-function that reaches the gods. O Sviṣṭakṛt, you have been the Hotṛ at the beginning; for the granting of wealth and the bestowing of riches, accept our word of homage and perform the sacrifice.

7 [4] (a) Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the possessor of bay horses; may Indra, accompanied by Pūṣan, eat the parched grains; may he, accompanied by Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, eat the groats; the scattered grain belongs to Indra, the cake to Mitra and Varuṇa, and the curd-mixture to the morning pressing; may Indra, accepting the offerings set forth, partake of them; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

(Ā) Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the possessor of bay horses. May Indra, accompanied by Pūṣan, eat the parched grains; may he, accompanied by Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, eat the groats. The scattered rice belongs to Indra; the cake belongs to Indra at the midday pressing. May Indra, accepting the offerings set forth, partake of the sacrificial cakes; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

(i) Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, the possessor of bay horses; let Indra, accompanied by Pūṣan, partake of the parched grains; let him, accompanied by Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, partake of the groats; let Indra partake of the scattered rice; let Indra partake of the cake of the third pressing, as it is set forth; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
(u) Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; let him enjoy the sacrificial cakes; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

(e) Let the Hotṛ worship Vāyu, who comes first, who arrives first, the drinker of Soma, the god who acts; may Vāyu come with his protection, may he enjoy it, may he partake; let him drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

(ai) Let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Vāyu, the worthy ones who lick [the offering], who are enriched with cattle and adorned with kine. By their bright, heroic, and swift teams, led by bulls, let the two heroes come with whip and horses at their head. May they perform their departure here and the unyoking for the believer. Thus may Indra and Vāyu enjoy, partake of, and drink the Soma; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

(o) Let the Hotṛ worship Mitra and Varuṇa, the noble rulers, the destroyers of enemies, who look down with a steady gaze, who are observant, most skilled in discerning the subtle, who perceive every element with unclouded vision, and who meditate upon the eternal Law (*ṛta*) as "the eternal Law. May Mitra and Varuṇa act thus; may they accept it, enjoy it, and drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Fifth Chapter, Section 987 (au):

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins, the Nāsatyas, who travel on long paths and follow the course of Rudra. May they, bringing desirable refreshments and strength between their two wheels, bring us excellent heroes. May the two men drive away our enemies from afar; O youthful ones, sprinkle this sacrifice with honey; may the Aśvins accept it thus, enjoy it, and drink the Soma—O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!

(aṃ) Let the Hotṛ worship Indra. May he come at every morning’s pressing; may Atri come from afar, from the wide mid-air, or from his own dwelling-place. For him, these bright Soma juices, dripping with sweetness, have been set forth for Indra; may he take pleasure in them, may he accept and drink the Soma. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship Indra—the eater of the portion and the drinker of the exclusive share of the midday pressing; the hearer of the call, the one who comes to the invocation, the protector of this prayer, the strengthener of the pressing sacrificer; may he fill both his flanks with the slayer of Vṛtra and with the bountiful gift. These bright and stirred Soma juices have been set forth for Indra; may he take pleasure in them, may he accept and drink the Soma. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

(ka) Let the Hotṛ worship Indra at the third pressing, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, the Vibhus, Vāja, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods; let him drink of the entire exhilarating draught. (ca) O Indra, eat and drink of the roasted grains and Soma; let your two bay steeds eat the grains and smell the dregs. O you who move among the people, drive forth your chariot! If they should ask you, "O husband of the wives, did you rejoice here?", then say to that pressing sacrificer: "What have I not bestowed upon him?"

"Excellent is the great power! O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice for that which the sacrificer has desired; let that come to pass! (Cha) "O Maghavan Indra, here indeed is your exhilaration. Tomorrow [announce] this [sacrifice] as being accompanied by the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Ṛjus, the Vibhus, the Vājins, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods; as a blessing, announce this to Indra, to Indra and Agni, to Mitra and Varuṇa, to the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Viśvedevas, the Brahmins, the Somyas, and the Somas. O Brahman, restrain your speech!"

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins with the Soma-offerings that have passed beyond the days; let them come three times around, and thrice, O Nāsatyas, grant us honor from there for the sake of the prize-winning strength, O Gods!
May he who is joined with the tawny-horsed one, dripping with ghee, be united with the Dawn and her ruddy steeds.
Together with the Etaśas, O Sūrya; together with their wondrous deeds, O Aśvins—may the Aśvins thus grant [our desires]. (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 1.27.7) Fifth Chapter, Verse 989.

"O Father and Mother, place for me flawless steps; may the sages recite flawless hymns. May Soma grant all things to be known; may Bṛhaspati recite the hymns of praise.
This *japa* (muttered prayer) is to be performed prior to the *ājya-śastra*. It is found here in AitBr 2.16; ĀśŚrSū 5.9; ŚāṅkhŚrSū 7.9.1; and TaitSaṃ 5.6.8.6.

Bṛhaspati shall recite the hymns and songs of praise (*ukthāmadāni*). "May he recite the flawless hymns" (*acchidrokthā*); "the seers (*kavayaḥ*) reciting the flawless hymns"—Soma [knows] all that is to be known. "The eager ones (*uśijaḥ*) have now fashioned the flawless steps"; Soma is the knower of all things. "The steps the eager ones have fashioned"—Soma [knows] all that is to be known. O divine immolators (*śamitāraḥ*), take hold! And you humans, lead [the victim] to the sacrificial doors, desiring the sacrifice for the two lords of the sacrifice.
Bring fire for him; spread the sacrificial grass. Let his mother give her consent, let his father, his uterine brother, and his companion of the same herd give their consent.

Place his feet toward the north; let him reach the sun with his sight, let him release his breath after the wind, his life-force into the atmosphere, his hearing into the quarters, and his body into the earth.
Strip off his skin in one piece before reaching the navel; extract the omentum from the flesh; ward off the internal heat within.

Make his breast like a hawk, his two arms like sacrificial knives, his forearms like *śalā*-sticks, his shoulders like *kaśyapa*-birds, his hips without a gap, and his thighs like the *sekaparṇa* plants. His two knee-bones are twenty-five ribs; lift them up in order and fashion his limbs accordingly. Dig out the receptacle for the undigested food (*uvadhya*) from the earth.
With the blood, unite the *rakṣas*.
Do not cause the rectum of this [sacrificial animal] to cry out as you go toward the wide space; let there be no crying among the immolators concerning the offspring and the progeny.
Perform the service well; perform the service with skill; perform the service, O ye who go toward it!

(1) When with his thick member he has struck down the small testicles, all the world trembles at him, as if at two donkeys dripping with semen. (2) When the unripe fruit becomes ripe, like the jujube (*karkandhu*), it bends down three times, moving like the springtime *taijana* plant. (3) When the gods have cast the *laṭābuka* fruit into the water, a woman is seen with you as its mate, like the eye of truth, like fortune (*bhaga*). (4) The great tree speaks to the horse’s erected member: "From such a tree as this, may we each take a winnowing-basketful of fruit. (5) The great tree indeed cried out; it sat upon the skin. (7) The great tree runs after the cuckoo with a pin. This *taijana* plant, when shaken, becomes a head-ornament. (8) The great tree runs after the great entrail as it runs. Guard these cows of his, who has prepared the rice-porridge for me. (9) Truly, the *vilva* is auspicious and great; the *udumbara* is great in the sacrifice.
